title: Historical Pilot - Verdantis

hero.intro: Up to five years of monthly Sentinel-2 median composites over the plot, reduced to three spectral indices server-side, then analysed locally: plot-average time series, a scrubbable month-by-month imagery view of the last year, and ERA5 temperature + precipitation overlays to sanity-check whether moisture drops track warm, dry spells.

timeseries.title: Time series (plot-average, monthly)
timeseries.lede: NDVI tracks vegetation vigour; NDWI and NDMI are two moisture-proxy formulations of the same underlying signal (broad vs. narrow NIR band) - shown side by side rather than picked between, since they're correlated but not identical.
timeseries.ndmi_desc: Moisture proxy, narrow-NIR (Sentinel Hub standard) formulation.

imagery.title: Monthly imagery, last year
imagery.lede: Whole-plot NDVI/NDWI/NDMI composites, scrub month by month - the same 12-month window as the Sector Explorer's "Last year" option, shown here since it's a single time series rather than a per-sector breakdown.

weather.title: Moisture vs. weather
weather.lede: NDWI merged against ERA5-based (Open-Meteo archive, no API key needed) monthly mean air temperature and total precipitation, for the same window and location.
weather.temp_desc: Pearson r ≈ 0.47 (NDWI) and ≈ 0.52 (NDMI) vs. temperature over the full history, printed by the script on every run - a sanity check, not a calibrated relationship.
weather.precip_desc: Pearson r ≈ 0.32 (NDWI) and ≈ 0.33 (NDMI) vs. total monthly precipitation over the full history - positive as expected (wetter months, higher NDWI), weaker than the temperature correlation above since a single month's rain total is a noisier proxy for canopy/soil moisture than temperature is.

note_html: Every threshold and correlation on this page is a pilot starting point. NDWI/NDMI "dry" thresholds (0.10 here) and the cloud-mask kernel sizes are copied from documented defaults, not independently tuned for this plot's species or soil - see the project README before using any number to drive a real decision.
